owner_brief: the owner, 2026-10-21: 'make sure every chest is instanced if it can be and make sure it has fun loot for every stage of the game. also make sure we dont put like moltres feather onto an instance chest in its tower, give the player something cool instead. also give out sigils for dungeons in areas.'
what_this_is: The CONTENTS of the per-player (Lootr) container tables cobblers:chests/<stage>/<kind>. The wiring of containers to tables is another unit's (datapack-content-dev). Each table rolls `rolls` times (uniform between min and max) over the weighted `entries`; `count` is uniform between its bounds. The sigil is a SEPARATE pool per table: one roll at `sigil.chance`, never a weighted entry, so it does not dilute the kind's loot.

stage_rule.rule: A container's stage is its AREA's encounter tier minus one (data/encounter_design.json: tier 1 -> s0 ... tier 8 -> s7, tier 9 Victory Road and the Rift -> s8, the Nether tiers 10-11 -> s8). A container BEHIND a gate takes the gate's badge count instead (a legendaries.json chamber opened at gym5_cleared -> s5; anything behind champion_cleared -> postgame). A town's containers take the town's arrival badges (gym N's town -> s(N-1); Pallet -> s0).
stage_rule.why: a Lootr table is fixed per container, but the player who opens it is not. Keying it to the area's tier means a chest pays what the area's wild Pokemon, Marts and counters already assume the player has; a player who arrives early gets the area's loot early, which is the cost the tier rule and the Marts already accept (data/traders.json tier_rule_caveats).
stage_rule.known_caveat: Sunset West (tier 5 -> s4) is reachable on foot at 0 badges (data/traders.json tier_rule_caveats), so a walker gets s4 loot there at cap 20. Accepted, as the Marts accept it: nothing in s4 is a catch item above the great ball (ultra balls start at s5).

sigil_rule.rule: every table carries one extra pool: one roll at the stage's `sigil.chance` giving ONE sigil of `sigil.band`, built by the builder from data/dungeons.json sigils.ladder (the sherd with custom_data {cobblers_dg_sigil:<band>b} as a BYTE, its item_name, colour, rarity and two lore lines). A sherd without that component is never taken by a rip (DUNGEONS.md 7.4 'The item').
sigil_rule.calibration: chance = target_per_player / containers a player opens in the stage. ASSUMED 30 containers opened per stage (no container count per stage exists in data/: the builder should measure it from its own wiring and re-derive chance = target / measured). Targets: 3.5 at s0 (no free first entry exists: data/dungeons.json free_first_entry.dungeons is [] while Q20 is open, so a found Soot Sigil is a new player's first run), 2.5 at s1-s7, 1.5 at s8 and postgame (netherite sigils, $900 and $1,708).
sigil_rule.excluded: NO container inside a rip dungeon carries the sigil pool: DUNGEONS.md 7.4 rule 5 and V16 ('a run cannot refund its own fee').
sigil_rule.sigil_is_not_income: no sell point buys a sherd (none is in data/bank.json buys or the base bank), so a found sigil is time saved (9 to 72 minutes of gathering, 7.4), never money

economy_checks.undercut: RULE-CHECKED against shop_first_sale for every entry; the exceptions are marked 'deliberate' in their why (revive at s3, ancient_great_ball at s1, ancient_ultra_ball at s4, sachet at s2): weight 3 or less and one stage early at most
economy_checks.arbitrage_buyers: RULE-CHECKED: the only sell points are data/bank.json buys (coal 4, raw_copper 2, copper_ingot 3, raw_iron 8, iron_ingot 9, lapis 4, raw_gold 20, redstone 2, diamond 120, ancient_debris 200, netherite_scrap 202, netherite_ingot 900, quartz 2), the base bank's survivor minecraft:elytra 25,000 (forbidden_everywhere), and the Produce Buyer under its per-player allowance (data/produce_buyer.json; unbuilt). Potions, held items, stones, TMs, berries, relic coins, food and sherds sell nowhere (base_removed / never_buy / not in buys).
economy_checks.fair_income: MEASURED from the tables below, by hand: expected bank value per opened container = sum over sellable entries of (weight / kind total) x mean count x price x mean rolls. Worst kinds, computed from the final weights: s0 mine $21 and s0 smith $15 against leg 1's $4,033 (0.5%); s4 mine $56 against leg 5's $21,433 (0.26%); s8 mine $118 and s8 smith $122 against Victory Road's $49,341 (0.25%); postgame smith $376 against the League's $175,051 (0.21%). Every container is opened once per player, so no loop exists by construction; the bound is that 30 containers of the worst kind pay at most about 15% of a leg, roughly one gathering hour at the stage's tier (data/bank.json effort_model). JUDGEMENT: the 1% per container ceiling is mine, not a rule in data/.
economy_checks.pickaxe_tier: RULE-CHECKED: no iron pickaxe before s2 (the deep tier opens on leg 3, played holding 2 badges, data/bank.json effort_model, DUNGEONS.md 7.4); no diamond before s4; no netherite before s8 (the Nether opens at badge 8, data/nether_gate.json)
economy_checks.progression_items: RULE-CHECKED: no Exp. Candy, IV candy, vitamin, mint, bottle cap, PP Up or Ability Capsule (dungeon-owned, DROPS_PROGRESSION_SPLIT.md 0.5). Rare Candy only at s8 and postgame, weight 1-5 (the owner's 'sparingly'; the dungeons pay it at bands 5-6). Ability Patch only postgame, weight 1-3. JUDGEMENT: Exp. Share at s1+ is allowed as a held item (the cap stops it overshooting, DROPS_PROGRESSION_SPLIT 0.2)

findings: ADR-007 decision 3 says a Lootr container never holds anything that matters once per player 'a TM, a patch, a key item, a summoning item', because a rebuild resets every container. This design puts TMs, an Ability Patch (postgame) and sigils in Lootr tables at low weight because the owner asked for TMs and sigils. If a re-apply or re-export resets Lootr state (the reason Lootr was HELD on 2026-10-09, docs/STATE.md line 153), every player can re-roll them. The owner should accept that or the TM and sigil entries should be removed. Key items stay out either way.

ADR-007 decision 4 says every per-player table is DETERMINISTIC (one pool per item, rolls 1, so every player gets the same). The brief asks for weighted rolls, so players get different loot. ADR-007 is still Proposed; this file follows the brief, and the ADR should be amended to match.

DUNGEONS.md 7.4 rule 2 says 'the only source is the recipe'. The owner's 2026-10-21 'give out sigils' amends that; 7.4 and the V16 sweep should be updated so a cobblers:chests table that pays a sigil is allowed (rip-interior containers still excluded).
DUNGEONS.md 7.4 rule 1 says the six sherds join data/bank.json never_buy; they are not there today. No effect now (no buyer carries them), but the guard the design describes is missing.

No money item exists: CobbleDollars has no currency item in the base pack's item index, and relic coins left the bank (base_removed). cobblemon:relic_coin stands in as a no-value collectible (Gimmighoul's stash).

The adopted towers' own barrels held themed loot (Zapdos: redstone, electric gems, a trident; Articuno: wind charges, ice gems, diamond boots; Moltres: blaze powder, fire gems; data/adopted_legendary_sites.json). site_overrides.rule: if the builder can name a table per site, a legendary site's containers use cobblers:chests/<stage>/legendary_<site> built from the stage's legendary_site entries PLUS these themed entries; if it cannot, they use the stage's legendary_site table, which is safe on its own.
